title: Strategic Reasoning and Language Models
question: How do language models reason about goals, strategies, and rules in interactive settings?
description: My research examines strategic dialogue, including inference of stance, goals, and strategy from conversational context. I design controlled evaluations to distinguish failures caused by missing information, constraints, and prompting assumptions, with strategic games providing a setting for studying decisions under explicit rules.

title: Persona Conditioning and Psychometrics
question: When does a persona change a model's behavior, rather than just its language?
description: I use psychometric inventories to translate persona descriptions into measurable trait profiles and strategic heuristics. This work examines the consistency of persona-conditioned behavior across prompts and model variants, and how those differences relate to performance in a strategic game.

title: Cognitive Modeling and Semantic Exploration
question: What can patterns in word association tell us about how people explore ideas?
description: My work combines natural language processing and graph analysis to characterize individual exploration styles across word-association tasks. Related collaborative work surveys behavioral, physiological, and cognitive measures of fatigue.

title: Document Retrieval and Legal Reasoning
question: How can retrieval and prompting support answers grounded in legal evidence?
description: I build retrieval and answer-synthesis pipelines over case corpora, from document segmentation and indexing to query-focused retrieval. Evaluation includes faithfulness, citation coverage, retrieval failures, and entailment mismatches. This work connects to the AMHR team's legal retrieval and entailment research in COLIEE.

title: Syntax-Guided Code Generation
question: How can explicit grammar constraints improve generated code?
description: I have worked on grammar-constrained transformer code synthesis, using a separate constraint layer to restrict token choices according to a formal grammar. Evaluation examines syntactic validity, exact-match behavior, and the failure modes introduced by different constraint settings.
